topic: Kubernetes ConfigMaps and Secrets — create and consume reference
linkedin_hook: Master Kubernetes configuration management with this essential ConfigMaps and Secrets cheatsheet!
linkedin_intro: As a DevOps engineer, I've worked with numerous teams to deploy and manage applications on Kubernetes. One common challenge we face is managing configuration data and sensitive information. To help you overcome this, I've put together a comprehensive cheatsheet on Kubernetes ConfigMaps and Secrets. This reference guide covers everything from basic commands to advanced techniques for creating and consuming configuration data in your Kubernetes clusters.

pro_tips: Use kubectl create configmap --from-file to create ConfigMaps from existing configuration files, and kubectl create secret generic --from-file to create Secrets from existing sensitive data files.
Utilize kubectl patch to update ConfigMaps and Secrets without having to recreate them, for example: kubectl patch configmap my-config -p='{"data":{"key1":"new-value"}}'
Leverage kubectl rollout to manage the rollout of new ConfigMaps and Secrets to your Deployments, for example: kubectl rollout restart deployment my-deployment --env=configmap/my-config
Use kubectl config set-context to set the default context for your kubectl commands, ensuring you're always working with the correct cluster and namespace.
